chunks: Saʿd narrated from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from al-Ḥasan ibn ʿAlī ibn Faḍḍāl, from ʿAbd Allāh ibn Bukayr, from ʿAlī ibn Ḥanẓalah, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:
I asked him about the last two rakʿahs: what should I do in them? He said: If you wish, recite Fātiḥat al-Kitāb; and if you wish, then remember Allah, for it is the same.
He said: I said, Then which of the two is more virtuous? He said: By Allah, they are equal: if you wish, you may recite tasbīḥ, and if you wish, you may recite.

key_terms.الرَّكْعَتَيْنِ الْأَخِيرَتَيْنِ: the final two units of the salat (prayer)
key_terms.سَوَاءٌ: equal in ruling and merit within this context
key_terms.فَاذْكُرِ اللَّهَ: engage in remembrance of Allah instead of recitation

ai.seo_question: In the last two rakʿahs of salat, should one recite Fātiḥat al-Kitāb or tasbīḥ?
ai.summary: This hadith states that in the final two rakʿahs of the prayer, one has a choice between reciting Fātiḥat al-Kitāb and engaging in dhikr of Allah through tasbīḥ. The Imam عليه السلام explicitly says that the two options are equal, indicating legal permissibility and equivalence in this context.
